rules.title: Duplicate named member is an error
rules.statement: Within a named-member list of a container, any non-empty name that appears more than once is a duplicate error (`duplicate <kind> '<name>' in <container>`). The anonymous binding name `_` (and empty names) may repeat freely.
examples: struct S { x: i32, x: i32 } // error: duplicate field 'x'

rules.title: Type-argument arity matching
rules.statement: A generic instantiation with parameter list P and argument list A is well-formed iff: if P's last parameter is a variadic pack (`T...`), |A| >= |P|-1 (the pack absorbs >=0 trailing args); otherwise |A| == |P|. Mismatch is an error stating the expected and actual counts.

rules.title: Type-args on a non-generic target rejected
rules.statement: Supplying >=1 type argument to a target whose type-parameter list is empty (non-generic) is an error: `<context> '<name>': not generic — cannot accept N type arg(s)`. (Diagnosed only after full type-parameter info is available, never during forward-declaration prepass.)
examples: struct S {} ; let x: S<i32>; // error: not generic

rules.title: Attribute `= value` must be an integer or enum variant
rules.statement: The right-hand value of an attribute `#[name = V]` read as an integer must be either an integer literal (`#[name = 123]`) or an enum variant path (`#[name = Enum::Variant]`, resolving to that variant's discriminant). Any other value form is an error; an unknown enum or unknown variant is also an error.

rules.title: Built-in attributes restricted to declared item kinds
rules.statement: Each compiler-recognised attribute is valid only on a fixed set of item kinds: `type_code`→{struct,datatype,enum,trait}; `zoned`→{struct,enum}; `datatype`→{struct}; `self_describing`/`rel_ptr`/`pinned`/`zone_mut`/`no_auto_drop`/`non_null`→{struct}; `borrow_carrying`→{struct,enum}; `annotation`→{struct,datatype}; `tag_dispatch`→{trait}; `metaprog_handler`/`no_mangle`/`fn_macro`/`token_macro`/`test`/`should_panic`/`ignore`→{fn}; `cfg`/`cfg_attr`→{all item kinds}; `repr`→{struct,enum}. Applying a built-in attribute to a disallowed kind is an error; an unrecognised name is treated as a user `#[annotation]` lookup.

rules.title: Struct/enum attribute flag vocabulary
rules.statement: The recognised struct/enum modifier attributes are exactly: `datatype`, `annotation`, `zoned`, `zone_mut`, `rel_ptr`, `self_describing`, `pinned`, `borrow_carrying`, `no_auto_drop`, `non_null`. A struct bearing `#[datatype]` or `#[annotation]` is promoted to the datatype pipeline.
rules.divergence: Logos-specific memory/zone attribute set; no Rust analogue.

rules.title: `#[repr(...)]` minimal recognised modes
rules.statement: `#[repr(...)]` is recognised only on structs (`transparent`) and enums (integer-discriminant width). Other repr modes are parsed and then rejected (no silent acceptance).
rules.divergence: Only `transparent` (struct) and integer-width (enum) repr supported; Rust's `C`/`packed`/`align`/etc. not yet.

rules.title: `#[should_panic]`/`#[ignore]` are `#[test]` modifiers
rules.statement: `#[test]` marks a free function as a test case; `#[should_panic]` and `#[ignore]` are modifiers valid only in combination with `#[test]`. All three apply to functions only.
rules.uncertainty: The 'only valid in combination with #[test]' constraint is enforced downstream, not in this unit (comment-stated).

rules.title: Unused type parameter warning (functions)
rules.statement: A function's declared type parameter that does not appear in its signature (parameter types, return type, or any trait-bound type-args) is warned as unused. Exemptions: variadic packs; const-generic params; names equal to `_` or beginning with `_`; and any param that itself carries a trait bound (the bound counts as a use). Lifetime parameters get the analogous unused-lifetime warning.
examples: fn f<T>(x: i32) {} // warn: type parameter 'T' is unused

rules.title: Trait bound naming an unknown trait is rejected
rules.statement: Every recorded type-parameter trait bound `T: Tr` must name a known trait; an unknown `Tr` is an error at the definition site. Exceptions: the Fn-family bounds (`Fn`/`FnMut`/`FnOnce`) and `Sized` are compiler-builtin and require no user-space trait declaration.
examples: fn f<T: Nonexistent>() {} // error: unknown trait

rules.title: Trait-bound type-argument arity
rules.statement: A trait bound `T: Tr<A...>` must supply type arguments matching Tr's type-parameter arity: if Tr's last param is variadic, |A| >= |params|-1; else |A| == |params|. A trait with no type params accepts no args. Mismatch is an error at the definition site.

rules.title: Recursive by-value type cycle detection
rules.statement: A struct or enum that (transitively) contains itself through only by-value field/payload edges (Struct, ZonedStruct, Enum) is a forbidden recursive-value type. Pointer, `&`, and `&mut` edges break the cycle (they lower to fixed-size pointers) and are permitted.
examples: struct S { next: S }      // error: recursive value type
struct S { next: Box<S> } // ok (pointer breaks cycle)

rules.title: Restricted-visibility marker accepts only pub(module)
rules.statement: An item's restricted-visibility marker `pub(W)` is accepted only when W is the contextual word `module` (module-linkage). Plain `pub` and no marker are non-module. Any other word (e.g. `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, `pub(in path)`) is rejected with the diagnostic "unsupported visibility `pub(W)` — only `pub(module)` is recognised".
rules.divergence: Logos has only `pub` and `pub(module)`; Rust's `pub(crate)`/`pub(super)`/`pub(in path)` are not recognised.

rules.title: `Sized` is a builtin no-op bound
rules.statement: `Sized` is a compiler-builtin marker auto-implemented for every size-known concrete type; a `T: Sized` bound is admitted as a no-op and accepted without trait lookup (matching Rust's implicit `Sized`). This positive-bound path is a no-op; the `?Sized` opt-out is handled elsewhere and IS supported (see `generic.bound.relaxed-only-sized`).
